Following the mid-August heatwave peak of 38.1°C at Kew Gardens, a shift to milder Atlantic air masses, increased cloud cover potential, and gusty southerly winds have moderated temperatures into the typical late-summer range, with limited diurnal heating expected under partly sunny conditions. Historical August averages near 22°C provide context, while the narrow spread between 23°C and 25°C outcomes reflects remaining uncertainty in boundary-layer moisture and exact timing of any frontal passage. Updated 48-hour model guidance before resolution will determine final positioning.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent official and model forecasts for Paris on August 25, 2026, converge on a daytime high near 26–28 °C, directly supporting the market’s leading outcomes of 27 °C (38 %) and 26 °C (24.5 %).** 

Multiple sources, including GFS-based guidance and European meteorological services, indicate partly cloudy skies with scattered showers or light rain that will limit insolation and cap temperatures. Afternoon peaks are projected around 26 °C in several runs (e.g., Weather-Atlas, MétéoSun) and up to 27–28 °C in others (WindBorne, select Météo-France analogs), consistent with the combined 76.5 % probability on those three bins. 

Climatologically, the 1991–2020 average high for August 25 in Paris is 24.5 °C; the current pattern reflects modest above-normal warmth from a south-southeasterly flow but lacks the clear, subsiding air needed for stronger heating. Light winds (generally 2–5 m/s) and high morning humidity further suppress the daily maximum. 

No major model runs released in the past 24 hours have shifted the envelope outside 25–29 °C, keeping lower-probability outcomes (30 °C+ or 25 °C and below) at single-digit or lower implied odds. Traders are therefore pricing the tight consensus around the most likely observed value under today’s guidance, with resolution expected once Météo-France or equivalent station data confirm the 24-hour maximum.
